Expectation1: Maintain regular communication with family members
Situation1: A family member has a new job and has shared some initial excitement about it with their relatives.
Expectation2: Follow all instructions provided by election officials
Situation2: Officials ask voters with last names A–M to move to a newly opened line, even though the original line is moving faster.
Story: I stood in the crowded community center, clutching my phone in one hand and my voter ID in the other. My daughter had just texted me, bubbling with excitement about her new job. She wanted to share every detail, and I knew how much it meant to her that I listened and responded right away. As a grandparent, I always tried to be present, to show my family that their joys and worries mattered to me. But just as I started to type a reply, an election official called out, “Voters with last names A through M, please move to the new line on the left.” My last name started with H. The new line was longer and slower, but the official’s voice was firm—this was the rule, and I was expected to comply. I glanced at the original line, moving briskly, and then at my phone, where my daughter’s message waited. I felt torn, caught between the duty to follow instructions as a responsible voter and the desire to be the supportive grandparent my family expected. My heart pounded as I hesitated, unsure which role to honor in that moment.
